record.context_brief: Semi-degree variant of the tournament split conjecture
record.original_question: Under the same high-dichromatic-number hypothesis on a tournament T, can one weaken one side of the conclusion by asking only that one of the two disjoint sets has dichromatic number at least k while the other has minimum out-degree and minimum in-degree both at least k? More precisely, must there exist disjoint sets A and B with A dominating B such that either χ⃗(A) ≥ k and min{δ⁺(B), δ⁻(B)} ≥ k, or the symmetric converse condition holds?

evidence.quote: What about if we ask for −→χ (A) ≥ k and min{δ+(B),δ−(B)} ≥ k or the converse ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A tournament is an orientation of a complete graph. For a digraph D, the dichromatic number χ⃗(D) is the minimum number of colors needed to partition V(D) into classes each of which induces an acyclic subdigraph. For a vertex v in a digraph D, let δ⁺(v) and δ⁻(v) denote its out-degree and in-degree, and define δ⁺(D) = min_v δ⁺(v) and δ⁻(D) = min_v δ⁻(v). For disjoint vertex sets A, B ⊆ V(T) in a tournament T, we say A dominates B if every arc between A and B is oriented from A to B. For X ⊆ V(T), write χ⃗(X) for the dichromatic number of the subtournament T[X], and δ⁺(X), δ⁻(X) for the minimum out- and in-degrees inside T[X].

Question. Does there exist a function f : ℤ_{>0} → ℤ_{>0} such that, for every positive integer k, every tournament T with χ⃗(T) ≥ f(k) contains two disjoint nonempty vertex sets A, B ⊆ V(T) with A dominating B for which at least one of the following holds:

 (i) χ⃗(T[A]) ≥ k and min{δ⁺(T[B]), δ⁻(T[B])} ≥ k, or
 (ii) min{δ⁺(T[A]), δ⁻(T[A])} ≥ k and χ⃗(T[B]) ≥ k ?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a 2023 digraphs workshop open-problems compilation as a posed variant of a tournament-splitting question regarding dichromatic number combined with semi-degree conditions. No published resolution was found in standard databases, and the problem appears to remain open.
